title: Finite residue extensions give finite maps to decent spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Call an algebraic space $X$ decent if every morphism $\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ from a field spectrum is quasi-compact: for every affine scheme $U\to X$, the scheme $U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}L$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Suppose $X$ is decent. Let $L$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $a:\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ a morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose its composite to $S$ has image a closed point $s\in S$ and the induced field extension $L/\kappa(s)$ is finite, meaning that $L$ is finite-dimensional over the residue field $\kappa(s)=\mathcal O_{S,s}/\mathfrak m_s$. Then $a$ is representable and finite: for every scheme $T\to X$, $T\times_X\operatorname{Spec}L$ is a scheme and its projection to $T$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Tag 08AL (lemma-finite-residue-field-extension-finite), finite-morphism assertion only. Decency is Tag 03I8 (definition-very-reasonable), equivalently Tag 03JV (lemma-UR-finite-above-x) condition (6).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-decent-quasicompact-monomorphic-points], every point of $X$ has a quasi-compact monomorphic field representative. Its affine-test quasi-compactness gives the scheme-test quasi-compactness assumed in [lem-sfb-decent-algebraic-field-image-closed]: for a scheme $T\to X$ and a quasi-compact open $V\subseteq T$, cover $V$ by finitely many affine opens $V_1,\dots,V_n$; the inverse image of $V$ in $T\times_X\operatorname{Spec}F$ is the union of the open subschemes $V_i\times_X\operatorname{Spec}F$, each quasi-compact by the affine test, hence is quasi-compact. The finite extension $L/\kappa(s)$ is algebraic: powers of any element are linearly dependent in the finite-dimensional vector space $L$. Thus [lem-sfb-decent-algebraic-field-image-closed] applies, since $s$ is closed, and gives a closed singleton $\{x\}=\operatorname{im}(a)$.

Apply [lem-sfb-decent-closed-point-field-immersion] to this closed point $x$. Obtain $i:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ with image $\{x\}$, a representable closed immersion. Its scheme tests are closed immersions, without any assumption that $X$ is a scheme.

source.place: Tag 0AHB (lemma-decent-space-closed-point), used for the closed field subspace in Tag 08AL

proof.text: Form $P=\operatorname{Spec}L\times_X\operatorname{Spec}K$. By the scheme-test assertion for $i$, its projection $p:P\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is a closed immersion. It is nonempty: the maps $a$ and $i$ represent the same point, so they agree after a common field extension, which supplies a field-valued point of $P$. By the affine description of closed immersions, $P=\operatorname{Spec}(L/I)$ for a proper ideal $I$ of the field $L$; hence $I=0$ and $p$ is an isomorphism. Composing its inverse with the other projection gives $b:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ with $a=i\circ b$.

source.place: Tag 08AL, field-subspace factorization; explicit pullback argument using the affine closed-immersion description

proof.text: The maps of residue fields along $\operatorname{Spec}L\xrightarrow{b}\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ give compatible inclusions $\kappa(s)\subseteq K\subseteq L$. A finite $\kappa(s)$-spanning set for $L$ also spans $L$ over $K$, so $L$ is a finite $K$-module. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-ring-map-finite] to $K\hookrightarrow L$ to conclude that $b$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 08AL, sentence beginning Of course and finiteness of the field-spectrum map

proof.text: For any scheme $T\to X$, the scheme $W=T\times_X\operatorname{Spec}K$ is a closed subscheme of $T$ by the assertion for $i$. The scheme $V=W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}L$ represents $T\times_X\operatorname{Spec}L$ by the fibre-product universal property and $a=i\circ b$. The map $V\to W$ is finite by base change of $b$, using [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]. The map $W\to T$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. Their composite is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. This proves representability and the required finiteness for every $T$; radiciality is not used.

source.place: Tag 08AL, final finite-composition argument; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03ZR (lemma-composition-integral), implemented on scheme tests
